summary30s: Vijayanagara ('City of Victory') was founded in 1336 on the banks of the Tungabhadra river by two brothers, Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty.
Ruins at Hampi were brought to light in 1800 by Colonel Colin Mackenzie, an engineer and surveyor of the English East India Company.
Krishna Deva Raya (reigned 1509-1529, Tuluva dynasty) was its greatest ruler: built Nagalapuram, composed Amuktamalyada in Telugu, and added the eastern gopuram to Virupaksha temple.
Abdur Razzaq noted seven lines of massive wedge-shaped mortarless stone fortifications that enclosed not just the city, but also agricultural tracts and forests.
The Royal Center housed the monumental Mahanavami Dibba (a massive platform for 10-day Navaratri/Dussehra rituals), Lotus Mahal, and the Hazara Rama temple.

coreConcepts.title: The Discovery of Hampi: Colin Mackenzie (1800)
coreConcepts.explanation: The ruins at Hampi were discovered in 1800 by Colonel Colin Mackenzie, an engineer and antiquarian in the East India Company who later became the first Surveyor General of India. He prepared the first survey map of the site. Much of his initial information was derived from the memories of priests of the Virupaksha temple and the shrine of Pampadevi. Later, in 1856, Alexander Greenlaw took the first detailed photographs of monuments, and epigraphists began collecting hundreds of inscriptions in Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, and Sanskrit.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Themes in Indian History Part II, Section 1
coreConcepts.examTip: Colin Mackenzie discovered Hampi in 1800 and became first Surveyor General of India in 1815.

coreConcepts.title: Rayas, Dynasties, and the Amara-Nayaka System
coreConcepts.explanation: Four dynasties ruled Vijayanagara: Sangama (1336-1485) -> Saluva (1485-1503) -> Tuluva (1503-1570) -> Aravidu (1570-c. 1646). Krishna Deva Raya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty. Under him, the empire expanded between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers (Raichur doab). The Amara-Nayaka system was a major political innovation: military commanders (Nayakas) were assigned territories (amaram) to govern. They collected taxes, maintained an army of horses and foot-soldiers, and sent an annual tribute to the king while appearing in person at court with gifts.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Themes in Indian History Part II, Section 2
coreConcepts.examTip: The term 'amara' is believed to be derived from the Sanskrit word 'samara', meaning battle or war (similar to Turkish amir).

coreConcepts.title: Fortifications and Agricultural Irrigation
coreConcepts.explanation: Abdur Razzaq, an ambassador sent by the ruler of Persia to Calicut in the 15th century, was greatly impressed by the fortifications. He recorded seven lines of forts. Crucially, the outer fortification wall encircled not only the city, but also agricultural fields, gardens, and forests. The walls were constructed using wedge-shaped stone blocks without mortar, held together by interlocking. Enclosing agricultural land prevented starvation during prolonged sieges. Water was channeled through the Kamalapuram tank and the Hiriya canal built by Sangama kings.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Themes in Indian History Part II, Section 3
coreConcepts.examTip: Foreign travelers amazed by fields inside forts: Abdur Razzaq (Persia), Domingo Paes, and Fernao Nuniz (Portugal).

coreConcepts.title: The Royal Centre, Mahanavami Dibba, and Sacred Centre
coreConcepts.explanation: The Royal Centre contained over 60 temples and secular pavilions. The 'Mahanavami Dibba' was a massive platform (11,000 sq ft base, rising 40 ft) on which the king watched the 10-day Mahanavami (Navaratri) festival: worship of the state horse, buffalo sacrifices, wrestling matches, and review of the army. Other secular structures included the Lotus Mahal (named by British officers; council chamber) and the Hazara Rama temple (reserved for the king and family, carved with Ramayana scenes). In the Sacred Centre stood the Virupaksha Temple (dedicated to Shiva, patron deity of Vijayanagara) and the Vitthala Temple (featuring the world-famous stone chariot and musical monolithic pillars).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Themes in Indian History Part II, Sections 4 & 5
coreConcepts.examTip: Kings signed royal orders as 'Sri Virupaksha' in Kannada script, claiming to rule on behalf of the god Virupaksha.

workedExamples.question:
Which of the following Persian ambassadors to Calicut in the 15th century was greatly impressed by the seven lines of fortifications enclosing agricultural fields in Vijayanagara?
(A) Duarte Barbosa
(B) Abdur Razzaq Samarqandi
(C) Fernao Nuniz
(D) Domingo Paes
workedExamples.explanation: Abdur Razzaq, an ambassador sent by the ruler of Persia to Calicut in the 15th century, described seven lines of forts that encircled not only the city, but also its agricultural hinterland and forests.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Identify the Persian envoy to Calicut: Abdur Razzaq Samarqandi.
Step 2: Recall his description: Recorded seven lines of fortifications encircling agricultural tracts.
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Foreign traveler testimony on urban planning and military defense.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify the Persian envoy to Calicut: Abdur Razzaq Samarqandi.

workedExamples.question:
The Amuktamalyada, a celebrated work on statecraft composed in Telugu, was authored by which Vijayanagara emperor?
(A) Harihara I
(B) Bukka I
(C) Krishna Deva Raya
(D) Rama Raya
workedExamples.explanation: Krishna Deva Raya, the most famous ruler of Vijayanagara (Tuluva dynasty), composed a work on statecraft in Telugu known as the Amuktamalyada.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Recall Krishna Deva Raya's literary patronage (Ashtadiggajas).
Step 2: His own masterwork in Telugu on kingly duties and statecraft is the Amuktamalyada.
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Royal literary masterworks and administrative texts.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Recall Krishna Deva Raya's literary patronage (Ashtadiggajas).
Step 2: His own masterwork in Telugu on kingly duties and statecraft is the Amuktamalyada.

commonTraps.misconception: Believing Vijayanagara fortifications used lime mortar to cement the granite blocks.
commonTraps.correctConcept: The stone blocks were wedge-shaped, which held them in place by interlocking without ANY mortar or cementing agent.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Questions ask 'Which mortar was used in Vijayanagara fortifications?' and options include Gypsum, Lime, Mud, and None.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: No mortar was used in the outer walls; stones were dry-fit and wedge-shaped.

commonTraps.misconception: Assuming the Battle of Talikota was fought against the Delhi Sultanate.
commonTraps.correctConcept: It was fought in 1565 against the combined armies of the DECCAN Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, and Golconda). Delhi was under Akbar at the time.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: Talikota = Vijayanagara vs Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar).

quickRevisionCard.title: Vijayanagara Empire High-Yield Summary
bulletPoints: Founded: 1336 by Harihara and Bukka (Sangama dynasty) on Tungabhadra river.
Discovery: 1800 by Colin Mackenzie (first Surveyor General of India in 1815).
Krishna Deva Raya (1509-1529): Greatest Tuluva king; acquired Raichur doab; built Nagalapuram; authored Amuktamalyada.
Fortifications: 7 concentric walls (Abdur Razzaq); wedge-shaped mortarless blocks enclosing agricultural fields.
Waterworks: Kamalapuram tank and Hiriya canal fed by Tungabhadra dams.
Royal Centre: Mahanavami Dibba (11,000 sq ft, 40 ft high; 10-day Dussehra festival), Lotus Mahal, Hazara Rama temple.
Sacred Centre: Virupaksha Temple (patron deity; kings signed as 'Sri Virupaksha' in Kannada), Vitthala Temple (stone chariot).
Amara-Nayaka System: Military chiefs governed territories (amaram), collected revenue, maintained troops, sent annual tribute.
Battle of Talikota (1565): Rama Raya defeated by Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda; city looted and abandoned.
Later Capitals: Shifted eastwards to Penukonda and later Chandragiri by Aravidu dynasty.

practiceQuestions.question: In 1800, who prepared the first survey map of the ruins of Hampi?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Colin Mackenzie, an engineer and antiquarian of the East India Company, brought the ruins of Hampi to light in 1800 and prepared the first survey map.

practiceQuestions.question: To which dynasty did Krishna Deva Raya, the most famous ruler of Vijayanagara, belong?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Krishna Deva Raya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty, which succeeded the Saluva dynasty in 1503.

practiceQuestions.question: What was unique about the fortifications of Vijayanagara as recorded by foreign travelers like Abdur Razzaq?

options.text: They were made entirely of imported Portuguese marble
They encircled agricultural fields, gardens, and forests within the outer lines
They had no gates or entrances, accessible only by underground tunnels
They were constructed with bricks baked in oil rather than stone

practiceQuestions.explanation: What was most significant about the fortifications was that they enclosed agricultural tracts and forests to prevent starvation during sieges.

practiceQuestions.question: In the Vijayanagara Empire, royal orders were signed in the Kannada script in the name of which deity?
practiceQuestions.explanation: All royal orders were signed 'Sri Virupaksha', usually in the Kannada script. Rulers claimed to rule on behalf of the god Virupaksha.

practiceQuestions.question: The massive ceremonial platform in the Royal Centre of Vijayanagara where the 10-day autumnal festival was celebrated is known as:
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Mahanavami Dibba was a massive platform rising from a base of about 11,000 sq ft to a height of 40 ft, where Navaratri rituals were staged.

practiceQuestions.question: Which canal built by kings of the Sangama dynasty drew water from a dam across the Tungabhadra to irrigate the cultivated valley separating the Sacred Centre from the Urban Core?
practiceQuestions.explanation: One of the most prominent waterworks was the Hiriya canal, which drew water from a dam across the Tungabhadra and irrigated the cultivated valley.

practiceQuestions.question: In the Amara-Nayaka system of Vijayanagara, the term 'amara' is believed to be derived from the Sanskrit word:
practiceQuestions.explanation: The term amara is believed to be derived from the Sanskrit word samara, meaning battle or war. It also resembles the Arabic amir, meaning noble or commander.

practiceQuestions.question: The Battle of Talikota (also known as Rakshasi-Tangadi), which led to the destruction of Vijayanagara, was fought in which year?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In 1565, the army of Vijayanagara under Rama Raya was routed at Talikota by the combined armies of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, and Golconda.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following temples in Vijayanagara was reserved exclusively for the king and his immediate royal family?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Hazara Rama temple was located in the Royal Centre; it was probably meant to be used only by the king and his family, with walls sculpted with scenes from the Ramayana.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The Raya Gopurams (monumental temple gateway towers) built by Vijayanagara kings often dwarfed the towers over the central shrines.
Reason (R): These colossal gopurams served as marks of imperial power and royal patronage, signalling the presence of the temple from vast distances.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Raya gopurams were towering statements of royal resources and devotion, visible from miles away. Both are true and (R) explains (A).
